jobs.title: Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
SaskTel is entering a defining period of change. As the organization accelerates its transformation into a modern tech forward communications leader, we are seeking a Chief Information Officer (CIO) who can bring clarity, courage and conviction to a division that sits at the centre of SaskTel’s future. This is a role for a leader who thrives in complexity, sees opportunity in legacy, and understands how to evolve a technology function into a true strategic engine for the business.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the President & CEO, the CIO is accountable for SaskTel’s enterprise technology strategy, digital modernization, cybersecurity posture, data governance, and the delivery of reliable, secure, and efficient technology services. The CIO also serves as SaskTel’s Chief Security Officer and holds enterprise accountability for data governance.
This leader will oversee a large, diverse team responsible for enterprise applications, infrastructure, cloud services, cybersecurity, architecture, and service delivery. This role requires a leader who can modernize a complex, legacy heavy environment and ensure they have a high-performing team who is willing and welcoming of the new technology horizon SaskTel is entering into.

The Mandate

For SaskTel, the role goes beyond providing telecommunications services. Technology connects Saskatchewan, strengthen communities, enables businesses and support the province’s economic growth. As technology continues to reshape how we live and work, it is increasingly central to Saskatchewan’s future.
This is not a caretaker role. It is a once in a career mandate to modernize, simplify, and elevate a technology environment that underpins every connection SaskTel delivers.

The Ideal Candidate

As the ideal candidate, you are a seasoned technology executive with a proven record of leading large, complex organizations through meaningful modernization. You bring deep expertise in enterprise systems, cloud transformation, cybersecurity, and data governance, paired with the leadership presence and elevate information services as a true strategic partner.
You have assembled 15+ years of progressive technology leadership experience, including significant time at the senior executive level, and a history of modernizing legacy environments, improving delivery performance, and driving cultural change. You understand how to strengthen execution, introduce modern development practices, and lead teams through ambiguity with clarity and confidence.
Academically grounded with a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, such as business, technology, or a related discipline and you are comfortable operating in regulated or public sector environments. Experience with large scale enterprise transformations, including OSS/BSS, CRM, ERP, or cloud native modernization, is highly valued.
Above all, you are courageous, collaborative, and forward looking. You bring the courage to challenge entrenched norms, the backbone to make risk based decisions, and the leadership maturity to reset a long standing operating model. You build trust quickly, communicate with executive presence, and bring the mindset and energy required to help SaskTel evolve.
If you are energized by meaningful transformation, if you thrive in environments where change is both necessary and possible, and if you want your work to matter beyond the balance sheet, this role offers a rare platform to make a lasting impact.

To Apply

For additional information or a confidential discussion, contact Leadership Source at 306-543-1666 or search@leadershipsource.ca.

Early applications are encouraged. The search may advance as strong candidates are identified.

At SaskTel, we believe in fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce that reflects the customers and communities we serve. We strive to create an environment where all employees feel empowered to contribute their unique perspectives, driving innovation and creativity, while advancing our efforts as Saskatchewan’s leading Information and Communications Technology provider.

jobs.title: Head of Finance
jobs.description:
Who We Are 🇨🇦

Tetra Digital Group is Canada’s leading institutional digital asset infrastructure provider.

As Canada’s first and only regulated digital asset custodian, we’ve built the institutional foundation the market demands. We’re backed by Urbana Corporation, National Bank, ATB Financial, Wealthsimple, Purpose Unlimited, Shakepay, Shopify, and Coinbase Ventures — some of the most consequential names in Canadian finance and fintech.

We operate two interconnected businesses: Tetra Trust, our regulated custody arm and CADD Digital, Canada’s first Canadian dollar-backed stablecoin issued by a regulated financial institution. It’s live on Base, Ethereum, and Tempo, with Solana next. CoinDesk and BNN Bloomberg covered it as the arrival of Canada’s first regulated digital dollar. 🚀

Here’s the problem we’re solving: Canada clears roughly $424 billion every business day, and much of the retail payment infrastructure underneath it was designed in the 1980s. Batch windows. Cut-off times. Weekends off. We’re building rails that settle continuously, programmatically, and under regulatory oversight.

We’re a team of ~30 people. We punch well above our size, and so does the opportunity ahead.

The Role 📊

You make sure the numbers behind Tetra hold up to anyone who checks them.

This is the senior finance seat at Tetra, and it’s genuinely hands-on. You’ll own accounting, FP&A, treasury, tax, audit, and regulatory reporting across all three businesses, and you’ll be the CEO and board’s partner on capital strategy, partnerships, M&A, and the next raise. You’ll work with a licensed trust company and a Canadian stablecoin company.  

You’ll be building the finance function for a business model that’s being defined in real time.

You’ll report to our [CEO], work directly with senior leaders of the firm, the board and its audit committee, and partner closely with our compliance, legal, engineering, and partnerships leads.

What You’ll Own 🎯

Capital, deals, and the next raise.
Own capital strategy across equity, debt, and strategic investment. Lead fundraising alongside the CEO, structure partnerships, M&A, and financing deals from first model to close, and manage the cap table and investor reporting for a shareholder base that includes some of Canada’s biggest banks and fintechs. The data room is ready before anyone asks for it. 💰
Board and executive partnership.
Be the key financial advisor to the CEO, executive team, and board on planning, controls, budgeting and audit committee materials.
Accounting and reporting under IFRS.
That includes consolidated reporting across Tetra’s entities, crypto-asset accounting and fair value measurement, accounting for CADD in circulation and the reserves behind it, revenue recognition for custody and issuance fees, and intercompany agreements and transfer pricing.
Reserve economics.
Reserve income is a core part of how CADD makes money, and it moves with every rate decision. With operations, compliance, and risk, you’ll shape the reserve investment policy: what we hold, where, at what duration, and with what liquidity buffer for weekend and holiday redemptions. You’ll model reserve income across rate scenarios and make sure the business still works when rates fall. 💵
Treasury and liquidity.
Account for corporate cash, runway, and liquidity across CAD, USD, and the digital assets among financial partners, counterparties, clients, issuers and holders. 
Regulatory capital and filings.
Trust company capital and liquidity requirements, regulatory financial reporting and FINTRAC, and readiness for evolving regulations. You will own audit readiness and support SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II work and reserve attestations.
Controls.
🔐 Design internal controls built for a regulated crypto business and a Canadian trust company, including, but not limited to, segregation of duties, maker-checker on payments and wallet movements. 
Tax, done right the first time.
Corporate income tax, GST/HST on digital asset and payment services, SR&ED, transfer pricing, and the new crypto-asset information reporting arriving under the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF).
Planning and Analysis.
📈 Budget, rolling forecast, and scenario models for each business line. Pricing, partner economics, and unit economics to propel our growth.
Finance systems, automated.
🤖 An ERP we won’t outgrow, a crypto sub-ledger, automated reconciliations, and AI-enabled reporting, and analytics.  
The team that comes next.
You’ll start with a small team and do plenty of the work yourself. As Tetra grows, you’ll hire, mentor, and lead a growing team.

What We’re Looking For 🔍

10+ years of progressive finance leadership, ideally a blend of experience in both regulated industries and high-growth startups, fintech, and institutional financial services.
Accountability for a finance function whose numbers were audited and regulated.
A bachelor’s degree in business administration, finance, or accounting, and a CPA or equivalent professional designation. 
Advanced IFRS, regulatory financial reporting, internal controls, and audit readiness. 
Capital and deal experience. Equity and debt raises, M&A structuring and due diligence, negotiations, and cap table management across complex corporate entities.
Multi-currency treasury, liquidity management and forecasting, and counterparty, operational, and regulatory risk assessment experience.
Digital asset fluency. Digital-asset accounting and fair value, integrating crypto and fiat rails, and how a stablecoin’s reserves, supply, and redemptions show up in the financial statements.
Canadian payments fluency. Interac, Lynx, EFT, and the Real-Time Rail, plus emerging standards like ISO 20022 and the Travel Rule.
Design thinking to build and improve billing systems, crypto sub-ledgers, and processes. 
Strategic thinking. You align finance strategy with where the business is going, and you can see how the finance function needs to scale before it breaks.
Strong communication skills. You can present to a board, client, regulator, and investor in the same week.
Comfort with ambiguity. You’ve led in fast-moving environments where the standards were still being written, and you built frameworks anyway.

Digital asset experience matters here, but it doesn’t have to come from a crypto company. If you’ve led finance at a bank, a payments processor, or a regulated fintech, and you understand how custody and stablecoins work, we welcome your application.

Extra points for: 🏆

You’ve led finance through a SOC 2 Type II, a reserve attestation, or a provincial or federal regulatory examination
You’ve worked on stablecoin, e-money, prepaid, or safeguarded-funds issuance, where every unit outstanding has to be backed by something real
You’ve run finance inside a trust company, bank, or other prudentially regulated institution, including regulatory capital reporting
You’ve completed capital raising efforts with strategic investors, banks and VCs
Experience with APIs, smart contracts, and blockchain analytics tools
You’ve built a finance function from scratch, including the first real ERP and sub-ledger implementation, not just run one someone else built
You’ve handled crypto tax and information reporting, including CARF readiness

What You Get 💼

💰 [$210,000–$265,000] base salary, commensurate with experience
🦷 Comprehensive health, dental, and paramedical coverage
🌱 $1,000 annual learning budget for finance, accounting, and digital asset certifications, courses, and conferences [plus professional designation dues]
🏢 3 days a week in office, with periodic travel 
🏝 Generous vacation allowances 
🇨🇦 A front-row seat to Canada’s digital dollar with a small, high-calibre team where your work is visible, your contributions are felt, and your growth is real

A Note on Fit 🧭

Tetra moves fast and the expectations are high. If you’ve spent your career waiting for a fully defined job description before getting started, this isn’t the right fit. If you are a leader who sees an opportunity and executes, who thrives in ambiguity, and takes ownership of outcomes, this role was built for you.
If that sounds energizing rather, we’d love to hear from you. 🤝
﻿

﻿ How to Apply ✍️

Submit your resume along with thoughtful answers to the application questions. Tell us who you are, what drives you, and why this role at this moment makes sense for you.
Tetra is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply and will provide accommodation throughout the hiring process upon request.

Your role as Director, Enterprise Account Management

Reporting to Melissa Trottier, Vice President, Customer Success, the Director, Enterprise Account Management has a mission to serve as a client advocate and trusted advisor for a highly strategic segment of Dialogue’s clientele, driving sustainable growth and ensuring long-term success.

This position requires an experienced leader, capable of managing strategic relationships, but above all, inspiring, mobilizing, and developing their team. The Director will play a key role in talent development, creating a collaborative environment, and achieving ambitious collective goals. They will be responsible for designing and implementing effective retention and engagement strategies, while ensuring our solutions optimally meet the complex and evolving needs of our clients. This leader brings a coaching and empowering management style that develops talent, fosters autonomy, and holds the team accountable to high standards.

The Director will be accountable for achieving a defined growth objective, ensuring the team generates sustainable and measurable value for both our clients and Dialogue. In close collaboration with the sales, partnerships, and marketing teams, this individual will act as the spokesperson for our most strategic clients, while strengthening team cohesion and performance to drive sustained growth.

What You'll Be Doing

Leading and growing a team of senior account managers, elevating their strategic advisor posture
Building and nurturing strategic relationships with key stakeholders, including C-suite and executive leaders
Supporting the team in designing value-based account strategies that drive retention, long-term expansion, and client advocacy, while identifying gaps and elevating the overall quality of execution
Representing Dialogue at industry events, conferences, and corporate functions to build lasting influence and credibility with HR market leaders, and bringing those insights back internally to inform our strategy
Influencing the strategic direction of our tech, clinical, and operational teams based on market signals, in order to evolve Dialogue's offering and stay anchored to real client needs
Acting as a central leader in aligning cross-functional teams to our clients’ complex needs, simplifying communication, and removing roadblocks

We'd love to hear from you if you have

5+ years of experience managing complex solutions with cross-functional teams
Proven experience negotiating and managing relationships with C-suite and senior executives, adopting a trusted advisor mindset
Excellent written and spoken communication skills in both French and English
Demonstrated ability to think strategically and critically, assessing opportunities and risks to develop relevant strategies
A track record of performance and success, showing a history of exceeding objectives
A strong bias for action and comfort with ambiguity
Mastery of a consultative account management approach: understanding the client’s business challenges before proposing a solution, and co-building value over time
Prior experience collaborating with a partner or broker network supporting shared clients, and understanding of tripartite relationships
Comfort with digital tools and a strong interest in technology and automation
Direct experience with human resources, employee benefits, the insurance industry, or corporate wellness programs is considered a strong asset

At Dialogue, your well-being is our priority

Benefits

Taking care of others also means taking care of our team! Depending on your role and employment status

, you could have access to the following benefits:

Access to the Dialogue app and virtual mental health support for you and your family
Benefits plan, a health spending account, dental coverage, and fitness reimbursement
4 weeks vacation, 9 wellness days, and 1 volunteer day
Hybrid work: 3 days/week in our Montreal or Toronto offices, excluding remote roles
Work abroad up to 4 weeks/year
Incentive plans, referral bonuses & RRSP matching
Learning via Coursera, external training budget & mentorship
Optional parental leave top-up

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Our client based in Burlington is seeking a hands-on, entrepreneurial CFO to partner closely with ownership and help scale a growing real estate development business. This is an opportunity for a finance leader who thrives in an evolving environment, enjoys building teams and infrastructure, and wants to play a key role in shaping the future of the organisation.
Client Details

Our client based in Burlington creates vibrant, enduring communities through the development of thoughtfully designed real estate projects that enhance the places where people live, work, and gather.
Description

Act as a strategic advisor to ownership on acquisitions, investments, capital allocation, and business growth initiatives.
Lead financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and cash flow management across the organisation.
Develop, refine, and maintain project pro formas, investment models, and business cases to support development and acquisition decisions.
Build and mentor a high-performing finance and accounting team while establishing scalable processes and controls.
Drive process improvement initiatives, including system implementations, replacements, and enhancements to support future growth.
Provide accurate and timely financial reporting, insights, and recommendations to ownership and key stakeholders.
Maintain a hands-on approach to accounting operations while balancing strategic leadership responsibilities.
Help navigate ambiguity, identify opportunities, and create structure in a dynamic, entrepreneurial environment.

MPI does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital status, or based on an individual's status in any group or class otherwise protected under applicable human rights legislation. MPI encourages applications from minorities, women, the disabled and all other qualified applicants
Profile

A successful 'CFO' should have:
Progressive finance leadership experience, preferably within real estate development, construction, private investment, family office, or closely held/private ownership environments.
Experience supporting acquisitions, investment analysis, and strategic business decisions.
Proven success leading process improvement, finance transformation, or ERP/system implementation initiatives.
Strong financial modelling and pro forma development capabilities.
Comfortable operating at both the strategic and tactical levels, from boardroom discussions to month-end review.
Demonstrated ability to build, develop, and lead teams through periods of growth and change.
CPA designation preferred.

Job Offer

Permanent CFO position in Burlington.
Salary commensurate with experience
Comprehensive benefits.

If this role aligns with your experience, we encourage you to apply.

About Dialogue

Dialogue is the #1 virtual care provider in Canada. By developing our Integrated Health Platform🅫, we provide exceptional online health and wellness programs (primary care, mental health, iCBT, EAP, and wellness) to organizations that want to improve the wellness of their employees and families.

When It Comes To Our Work, We Set The Bar High. Together, We’re Transforming Health And Helping Millions Improve Their Well-being. We’re Firm Believers That Great People Don’t Settle On

Impact
Community
Growth
Excellence

Feel like you can make a difference? Good news, we saved you a seat!

Come as you are. As a proud equal-opportunity employer, Dialogue is dedicated to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace for everyone. Qualified applicants will be considered regardless of citizenship, ethnicity, race, colour, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, age, or veteran status. Applicants who require specialized accommodation are encouraged to contact accessibility@dialogue.co .

AI Disclosure Statement

To ensure an efficient and fair review process, we utilize artificial intelligence tools to assist in the initial screening and assessment of applicants for this role.

⚠️ Recruitment Fraud Notice

Dialogue only contacts candidates through official @dialogue.co

email addresses. We never request payment, gift cards, or personal financial information at any stage of hiring, and we never extend an offer without a structured interview process. All open roles are listed exclusively at dialogue.co/en/careers

. If you receive a suspicious communication claiming to be from Dialogue, do not respond — report it to jobs@dialogue.co

and verify the role on our official careers page.

Your role as Director, Enterprise Account Management

Reporting to Melissa Trottier, Vice President, Customer Success, the Director, Enterprise Account Management has a mission to serve as a client advocate and trusted advisor for a highly strategic segment of Dialogue’s clientele, driving sustainable growth and ensuring long-term success.

This position requires an experienced leader, capable of managing strategic relationships, but above all, inspiring, mobilizing, and developing their team. The Director will play a key role in talent development, creating a collaborative environment, and achieving ambitious collective goals. They will be responsible for designing and implementing effective retention and engagement strategies, while ensuring our solutions optimally meet the complex and evolving needs of our clients. This leader brings a coaching and empowering management style that develops talent, fosters autonomy, and holds the team accountable to high standards.

The Director will be accountable for achieving a defined growth objective, ensuring the team generates sustainable and measurable value for both our clients and Dialogue. In close collaboration with the sales, partnerships, and marketing teams, this individual will act as the spokesperson for our most strategic clients, while strengthening team cohesion and performance to drive sustained growth.

What You'll Be Doing

Leading and growing a team of senior account managers, elevating their strategic advisor posture
Building and nurturing strategic relationships with key stakeholders, including C-suite and executive leaders
Supporting the team in designing value-based account strategies that drive retention, long-term expansion, and client advocacy, while identifying gaps and elevating the overall quality of execution
Representing Dialogue at industry events, conferences, and corporate functions to build lasting influence and credibility with HR market leaders, and bringing those insights back internally to inform our strategy
Influencing the strategic direction of our tech, clinical, and operational teams based on market signals, in order to evolve Dialogue's offering and stay anchored to real client needs
Acting as a central leader in aligning cross-functional teams to our clients’ complex needs, simplifying communication, and removing roadblocks

We'd love to hear from you if you have

5+ years of experience managing complex solutions with cross-functional teams
Proven experience negotiating and managing relationships with C-suite and senior executives, adopting a trusted advisor mindset
Excellent written and spoken communication skills in both French and English
Demonstrated ability to think strategically and critically, assessing opportunities and risks to develop relevant strategies
A track record of performance and success, showing a history of exceeding objectives
A strong bias for action and comfort with ambiguity
Mastery of a consultative account management approach: understanding the client’s business challenges before proposing a solution, and co-building value over time
Prior experience collaborating with a partner or broker network supporting shared clients, and understanding of tripartite relationships
Comfort with digital tools and a strong interest in technology and automation
Direct experience with human resources, employee benefits, the insurance industry, or corporate wellness programs is considered a strong asset

At Dialogue, your well-being is our priority

Benefits

Taking care of others also means taking care of our team! Depending on your role and employment status

, you could have access to the following benefits:

Access to the Dialogue app and virtual mental health support for you and your family
Benefits plan, a health spending account, dental coverage, and fitness reimbursement
4 weeks vacation, 9 wellness days, and 1 volunteer day
Hybrid work: 3 days/week in our Montreal or Toronto offices, excluding remote roles
Work abroad up to 4 weeks/year
Incentive plans, referral bonuses & RRSP matching
Learning via Coursera, external training budget & mentorship
Optional parental leave top-up
